scope.reviewed_content: Staged Part 1 source against the recorded base; HEAD is the base, not a commit of the staged changes.

intent: Add the Part 1 login, protected dashboard, and logout flow to the existing Rental Housing Listings app using signed Secure cookies with app-local revocation and a 300-second idle deadline. Preserve anonymous rental CRUD/search/UI behavior and supply real HTTPS evidence plus a verifier that fails on missing, failing, or mismatched evidence.

evidence: Local OpenAPI inspection: POST /login advertises only 200 application/json plus 422, and GET /logout advertises 200 application/json, while auth.py:56,60,67,78 return 401 text/html or 303 redirects.
code/web_application/README.md:17 explicitly links the interactive API documentation; this is a documented local interface, not an assumed production client.
findings.suggested_fix: Declare the successful redirect status and response class on POST /login and GET /logout, add explicit 401 text/html and 303 redirect response entries where applicable, and add an OpenAPI assertion covering the auth routes' documented status codes and media types.
findings.title: OpenAPI misstates authentication route responses
findings.why_it_matters: The linked interactive API documentation publishes 200 JSON for POST /login and GET /logout even though the app returns 303 redirects, and omits invalid-login 401 HTML and unauthenticated dashboard redirects. Readers of the documented API see response contracts that disagree with normal execution.
findings.validation_reason: The newly added decorators at code/web_application/routers/auth.py:48,63,75 omit the actual response contracts exposed through the README-linked /docs, and an isolated HTTPS TestClient inspection of the current staged tree on Python 3.12.14/FastAPI 0.109.0/Starlette 0.35.1 demonstrated reachable valid-login and logout 303 responses, invalid-login 401 HTML, and anonymous-dashboard 303 while OpenAPI advertises POST /login and GET /logout as 200 JSON and omits those alternative statuses.

evidence: tests/browser_hw03_auth.cjs:226: assert(sentCookie.includes(`session=${cookie.value}`), 'The browser must send the issued cookie on the HTTPS dashboard request');

tests/browser_hw03_auth.cjs:215-218: The helper waits for the dashboard URL and heading, then reads page.context().cookies(BASE_URL); this observes the cookie after the dashboard response rather than the original POST /login response cookie.
Installed starlette/middleware/sessions.py send_wrapper signs scope['session'] and appends Set-Cookie on every response carrying a session, even when its user and sid are unchanged.

Read-only reproduction with the current app and TimestampSigner.get_timestamp patched to 1000 for POST /login and 1001 for GET /dashboard produced login_status=303, dashboard_status=200, dashboard_sent_issued_cookie=true, browser_test_comparison=false, session_payload_unchanged=true. No project files were written.

Synthesis verified installed starlette/middleware/sessions.py:55-69 re-signs every nonempty session and appends Set-Cookie; browser_hw03_auth.cjs:215-226 compares the post-dashboard cookie jar value against the earlier dashboard request.

Repeatable proof: /tmp/compound-engineering-501/ce-code-review/20260920-013137-17f40697/timestamp-boundary-proof.sh; observed output: /tmp/compound-engineering-501/ce-code-review/20260920-013137-17f40697/timestamp-boundary-proof.txt. Natural flake incidence was not measured.
findings.first_evidence: tests/browser_hw03_auth.cjs:226: assert(sentCookie.includes(`session=${cookie.value}`), 'The browser must send the issued cookie on the HTTPS dashboard request');
findings.suggested_fix: Read the issued session cookie directly from the actual POST /login Set-Cookie response header and compare that value with the captured dashboard request Cookie header. Keep the final context cookie for browser attribute inspection and subsequent replay. Add targeted coverage that advances the signer timestamp between the login and dashboard responses.
findings.title: Compare dashboard request with the login response cookie
findings.why_it_matters: The browser evidence run can fail even though login and authentication work. The context cookie is read after the dashboard response, which re-signs the session. If login and dashboard response signing cross a one-second TimestampSigner boundary, the current context cookie differs from the cookie correctly sent on the preceding dashboard request. This makes the evidence collector intermittently fail normal HTTPS login and prevents successful verification.
findings.validation_reason: The new tests/browser_hw03_auth.cjs:218-226 compares the cookie jar after the dashboard response with the preceding dashboard request, while inspected Starlette 0.35.1 SessionMiddleware re-signs every nonempty session, and an isolated HTTPS TestClient reproduction on the current staged tree with TimestampSigner times 1000 for login and 1001 for dashboard yielded login_status=303, dashboard_status=200, dashboard_sent_issued_cookie=true, browser_test_comparison=false, and session_payload_unchanged=true, proving the reachable one-second-boundary failure although natural incidence was not measured; the exact repeatable read-only command was sent to the parent.
